subject: Kinetic Analytics redline: telemetry & runtime-access — routing to Product/Security
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@kinetic.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kinetic DPA comments (telemetry + runtime access)

Hi Marissa,

Attached is Kinetic's redline to your standard DPA. Two items are blocking legal sign-off on our side and we need your position before next week:

- Section 4.2 (Telemetry): we need explicit limits on telemetry collection and retention. Kinetic requires that telemetry related to inference outputs and prompts be pseudonymized and retained no longer than 45 days unless expressly required for safety.
- Section 7.1 (Runtime access/subprocessors): your original language implies runtime access for analytics/export of aggregate inference logs and use of third-party analytics subprocessors with potential access to KV cache snapshots. We need clarity and hard constraints: no raw prompt/output export, and subprocessors must be disclosed in writing.

We attached our marked-up DPA (Kinetic_DPA_redline.pdf). Can you route this to the team that owns product/security sign-off? We have a deadline from procurement on 2027-08-06.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Legal Counsel, Kinetic Analytics

Subject: Re: Fwd: Kinetic DPA comments (telemetry + runtime access)

Thanks Marissa — high level thoughts from Product.

1) Telemetry pseudonymization + retention
- Pseudonymization: we can stop storing direct prompt/output text in permanent logs if we implement hashing/prefix tokenization, but this impacts several features (debugging, quality monitoring, evals). We can provide aggregated metrics and hashed identifiers for troubleshooting.
- Retention: 45 days is reasonable for aggregated telemetry; 30 days is easier operationally for some workloads. We should push back to 30/45 tradeoff in contract language (offer 45 days with an option for 30 for standard tiers).

2) Runtime access / KV cache
- We cannot export raw KV cache snapshots for customers; those contain model internals and are technically complex. For analytics, we can export aggregated token-level metrics (latency, token counts, model variant used) but not raw prompts/outputs. If Kinetic insists on raw-session exports, the supported path is Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with a scoped export process and a higher security/pricing tier.

3) Suggested language snippets (draft):
- "Redwood will collect telemetry necessary to operate and improve the service. Telemetry excludes raw prompt or complete inference output intended for export. Telemetry may be pseudonymized and retained no longer than 45 days for troubleshooting and service quality purposes."
- "Customer data exported for analytics will exclude raw prompts and full inference outputs unless otherwise agreed in writing and executed as a Private deployment with mutually agreed security controls."

Open questions for Security: can we commit to disclosure of analytics subprocessors in writing (not public list) and provide notification windows? And can Security propose a minimal KMS/audit package for Enterprise private option?

I'll prepare a redline response if Security confirms acceptable mitigations.

—Olga
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@kinetic.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Kinetic DPA comments (telemetry + runtime access)

Risk summary and mitigation proposals:

- Risk: Unrestricted telemetry export or KV cache snapshots could expose PII or model internals.
- Mitigation A (Standard hosted): Accept pseudonymized telemetry + retention window (we recommend 30 days for hosted tiers). Limit telemetry exports to aggregated metrics; deny raw prompt/output export. Provide written notification of analytics subprocessors and an obligation to disclose any new subprocessors 30 days before onboarding. Provide SOC2 Type II and penetration test summary.
- Mitigation B (Enterprise private): For customers requiring raw/session exports, require Redwood Private or dedicated VPC deployment, explicit contract SOW for export process, dedicated KMS keys (customer-managed), and annual audit sampling. Additional security fee applies.

We can produce a short "security_risk_summary.docx" for legal that outlines these options and recommended contract language. If Product accepts the 30-45 day window trade and the prohibition on raw exports for hosted customers, we can sign off on a clause that reads similar to Olga's draft.

Attachments: security_risk_summary.docx

-Jonas
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kinetic DPA comments (telemetry + runtime access) — options and next steps

Hi Sara — thanks for the redline and the patience. Internal product & security reviewed and we propose two workable paths so procurement can pick the one that matches risk appetite and budget:

Option 1 — Hosted (faster, standard):
- Telemetry: Redwood will collect operational telemetry but will exclude raw prompt or full inference output from exportable logs. Telemetry can be pseudonymized and retained up to 45 days (we prefer 30 for standard customers; happy to give 45 for this contract).
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide written disclosure of analytics subprocessors during contracting and agrees to notify Kinetic 30 days before adding a new subprocessor that may process telemetry.
- Security deliverables: SOC2 Type II report and penetration test summary.

Option 2 — Enterprise Private (for raw/export needs):
- Private deployment / VPC with customer-managed KMS, scoped export SOW, and annual audit sampling. This path allows session-level exports under strict controls and a higher monthly fee.

Next steps: Please confirm which option Kinetic prefers and any specific language you need. Attached is a first-pass response redline (redline_response_v1.pdf) for legal. We can follow with final contract language if you confirm the option.

We aim to finalize language by 2027-08-06 per your procurement deadline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
